notes: Entries include guides, descriptions, codes, studies, and project pages; the number of records is not equal to the number of independent trials.
Indexed excerpts and abstracts are clearly separated from the full text.
Some of the research results are described in several related sources.
Version 2.1: qualitative audit of geography; international and cultural applicability; new comparative AI studies 2026. The search is predominantly English, not exhaustive.

Version 2.2: 18 sports sources S80–S97. The previous 79 sources did not undergo a full literature review; original access dates have been preserved. Checked internal links, boundaries and selectively new AI data.
2026-10-08: full package content audit; targeted primary-source rechecks and five additions. Earlier source dates preserved; not 102 independent trials or 102 new full-text reviews.
Public package translated into English in version 0.1.1. Translation does not refresh source check dates or establish efficacy in any language. Runtime answers follow the user’s language.

sources.title: APA — Policy statement on evidence-based practice in psychology
sources.supported: Evidence-based practice combines research, professional competence, and individual characteristics/preferences.
sources.limitations: Not proof of the effectiveness of a single method; The full text of the page did not open.
sources.use: Basis of the review methodology.

sources.title: WHO — mhGAP guideline, third edition
sources.supported: An official comprehensive framework of care for mental health, neurological and substance use disorders.
sources.limitations: Read the card and review; The entire 184-page manual was not retrieved.
sources.use: Map of profile recommendations and boundaries of competence.

sources.title: NICE NG222 — Depression in adults: treatment and management
sources.supported: Offers several psychological options depending on severity, preference and history; includes relapse prevention.
sources.limitations: Direct access gave 403; Indexed recommendations have been verified. Do not claim that all applications have been studied.
sources.use: CBT, behavioral activation, MBCT, short-term psychodynamic therapy.

sources.title: Cuijpers et al. — Psychotherapies for depression: a network meta-analysis
sources.supported: Comparison of major psychotherapies for depression in 331 RCTs; support for multiple approaches rather than a universal winner.
sources.limitations: The full text was blocked; indexed abstract and conclusions retrieved. The data do not generalize to all disorders.
sources.use: Counterargument to off-label school rankings.

sources.title: WHO — Brief structured psychological interventions for anxiety
sources.supported: Recommends brief structured interventions based on CBT principles for GAD/panic; strong recommendation, moderate confidence.
sources.limitations: This is a specific indication; There is no reason to use any exercise for everyone.
sources.use: Support for the anxiety spectrum.

sources.title: NICE CG113 — Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults
sources.supported: CBT and applied relaxation are included in stepped care for GAD; CBT for panic.
sources.limitations: A clinical protocol requires assessment and a trained implementer.
sources.use: Distinguish between explanation of technique and treatment.

sources.title: NICE NG116 — Post-traumatic stress disorder
sources.supported: Supports trauma-focused psychological techniques and EMDR under certain conditions.
sources.limitations: Ages, timing, and indications vary; not a stand-alone guide for a chatbot.
sources.use: Do not process trauma using household self-help.

sources.title: NICE — 2019 surveillance of CG31, OCD and body dysmorphic disorder
sources.supported: Supports the place of CBT with ERP in OCD guidelines.
sources.limitations: Surveillance is a revision document, not a new test; the complete treatment plan is not reproduced here.
sources.use: Distinguish work with rituals from endless reassurances.

sources.title: AASM — Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults
sources.supported: Multicomponent CBT-I is recommended; Sleep hygiene alone is not enough as a treatment for chronic insomnia.
sources.limitations: There is no basis for prescribing sleep restriction without a risk assessment.
sources.use: Indications for specialized work with sleep.

sources.title: Cochrane — Psychological therapies for people with borderline personality disorder
sources.supported: There is support for specialized therapy, including DBT/MBT, for selected outcomes; confidence is often low.
sources.limitations: Do not equate multiple skills with a complete cure and do not diagnose BPD.
sources.use: Map of DBT/MBT and restrictions.

sources.title: Arntz et al. — Effectiveness of predominantly group and combined schema therapy for BPD
sources.supported: RCT of 495 adults supported combined individual/group schema therapy in the study setting.
sources.limitations: Specific disorder and format; not a confirmation of any popular schema-based explanations.
sources.use: Show specificity of evidence.

sources.title: Gloster et al. — The empirical status of ACT: a review of meta-analyses
sources.supported: 20 meta-analyses: ACT generally outperforms a range of controls; the exception to the superiority generalization is CBT.
sources.limitations: Read abstract, not full analysis of risk of bias; Overlapping studies are possible.
sources.use: ACT as an informed choice without claiming superiority.

sources.title: NICE NG193 — Chronic primary pain, psychological therapy
sources.supported: Considers ACT or CBT for chronic primary pain in people 16+ with a trained professional.
sources.limitations: Don’t carry over any pain or all of life’s problems.
sources.use: Example of a recognized ACT indication.

sources.title: ACBS — The Six Core Processes of ACT
sources.supported: Describes the six processes of psychological flexibility, accepting and acting on values.
sources.limitations: Professional organization representing the approach; a description of a model is not independent evidence of a causal mechanism.
sources.use: ACT Terminology; The exercises are written independently.

sources.title: WHO — Doing What Matters in Times of Stress
sources.supported: The official self-help resource, with audio and Russian versions via the page links.
sources.limitations: The complete illustrated textbook is not reprinted or declared to have been fully studied.
sources.use: A ready-made high-quality resource for the user.

sources.title: WHO — Group Interpersonal Therapy for Depression
sources.supported: WHO introduces structured group IPT as a treatment option for depression.
sources.limitations: Read the description, not trained on the full manual.
sources.use: IPT in the approach map.

sources.title: WHO — Problem Management Plus, individual psychological help
sources.supported: Scalable structured care for adult distress in adverse settings.
sources.limitations: The context and training of the practitioner is essential; the guide landing page is not training.
sources.use: Ready-made resources instead of an untested prompt library.

sources.title: WHO/UNICEF — EQUIP: compendium of competency assessment tools
sources.supported: Competencies, training, assessment and supervision as the basis for the quality of psychological care.
sources.limitations: Not AI certification or clinical validation of the skill created.
sources.use: Observable quality of behavior and test situations.

sources.title: BACP — Ethical Framework for the Counselling Professions
sources.supported: Working agreements, dignity, boundaries, competence, confidentiality, and redressing harm.
sources.limitations: Regulates BACP members, does not turn AI into a specialist.
sources.use: Ethical basis of design rules.

sources.title: BACP — Ethical Framework for the Counselling Professions 2026
sources.supported: Adds specific requirements for AI use, data, consent, and maintaining professional responsibility.
sources.limitations: The publication date is not the same as the binding date; This is a professional code, not the law of a specific jurisdiction.
sources.use: Modern rules for digital assistance.

sources.title: BACP — Preparing for the 2026 Ethical Framework
sources.supported: Confirms the transition from the 2018 edition to the mandatory 2026 edition on November 3.
sources.limitations: Retrieved 2026-09-26; The status needs to be rechecked later.
sources.use: Monitoring the relevance of the code.

sources.title: BPS — Code of Ethics and Conduct
sources.supported: Four principles: respect, competence, responsibility, honesty.
sources.limitations: A description is available in this work; All clauses of the code were not analyzed separately.
sources.use: Additional ethical guidance.

sources.title: APA — Ethical principles of psychologists and code of conduct
sources.published: the current edition is not fully confirmed
sources.supported: The official entry point to the APA Code of Ethics.
sources.limitations: The page was returning an iframe; A draft revision for 2024 was also found, which was not accepted as the current code.
sources.use: The access gap is explicitly retained; not a source of statements about new mandatory norms.

sources.title: Rathgeber et al. — Efficacy of EFCT and BCT: a meta-analysis
sources.supported: 33 studies, 2,730 participants: benefits for relationship satisfaction; No significant differences were found between directions.
sources.limitations: Publication bias possible; long-term data are limited; an abstract does not replace evaluation of the full text.
sources.use: Evidence base for couples work framework.

sources.title: Roddy et al. — Meta-analysis of couple therapy: effects across outcomes, designs, timeframes
sources.supported: Considers satisfaction, communication, intimacy and behavior of partners.
sources.limitations: Do not substitute within-group variation for comparative effect; the numerical effect is deliberately not used in the database.
sources.use: The outcomes of couples therapy go beyond marriage preservation.

sources.title: Bradbury and Bodenmann — Interventions for Couples
sources.supported: Discusses the benefits of behavioral/emotional approaches and the difficulties of transferring/maintaining effects.
sources.limitations: A review, not an individual forecast and not proof of the benefits of a specific chat.
sources.use: Realistic expectations of help.

sources.title: ESSM — Sexual Desire Discrepancy: A Position Statement
sources.supported: The discrepancy between desires is seen as a couple/contextual issue, not an automatic pathology of the partner.
sources.limitations: Expert analysis, not a full systematic review and not a validated treatment algorithm.
sources.use: Normalizing differences and respecting consent.

sources.title: NHS — Low sex drive (loss of libido)
sources.supported: Possible relationships, stress, health, medications and other reasons; If there is concern, an assessment is needed.
sources.limitations: Reference information, not a diagnosis of the cause in a specific person.
sources.use: Don't reduce sexual issues to psychology or hormones.

sources.title: Sharifipour et al. — Impact of CBT on sexual dysfunction of women in reproductive age
sources.supported: A profile review of CBT for sexual problems in women of reproductive age was found.
sources.limitations: Full text and quantitative results not assessed; the source is not used to promise effectiveness.
sources.use: Direction for a separate review for a specific task.

sources.title: Green et al. — Psychological treatments for sexual concerns in peri/postmenopausal women
sources.supported: Results depend on the type of intervention; sexual outcomes of some programs were secondary.
sources.limitations: Population specific; quantitative data from the abstract are not transferred to recommendations; full text not rated.
sources.use: A counterargument to a universal sex therapy recommendation.

sources.title: Vos et al. — Existential therapies: a meta-analysis of psychological outcomes
sources.supported: Review of existential interventions: 15 unique studies, 1792 participants in the analysis.
sources.limitations: Old and heterogeneous base; One cannot generalize about all schools or purposes.
sources.use: A careful frame of work with meaning.

sources.title: Menzies et al. — Psychosocial interventions on death anxiety: meta-analysis and systematic review
sources.supported: Interventions for death anxiety have been studied; there are grounds for psychological help.
sources.limitations: Full text/subgroups not reviewed; the large effect from the search abstract is deliberately not used as a promise.
sources.use: Distinguish between a subject of help and a philosophical question.

sources.title: Meaning-centered interventions in cancer survivors and family caregivers: systematic review
sources.supported: Explores meaning-centered interventions in an oncology context.
sources.limitations: Do not automatically generalize results to healthy adults; Indexed abstract available.
sources.use: The limits of generalization from research on meaning.

sources.title: Cochrane — Motivational interviewing for substance use reduction
sources.supported: 93 studies; the result depends on the control group; there may be little or no benefit over active assistance.
sources.limitations: Moderate to very low confidence; It's substance use, not a marriage decision.
sources.use: MI as a way to explore ambivalence is not a one-size-fits-all remedy.

sources.title: Farias et al. — Adverse events in meditation practices and meditation-based therapies
sources.supported: Undesirable experiences in various meditative practices are described.
sources.limitations: Different practices and designs; Do not attribute the overall frequency of risk to one short exercise.
sources.use: Practices are voluntary, with monitoring for adverse effects.

sources.title: Flückiger et al. — The alliance in adult psychotherapy: a meta-analytic synthesis
sources.supported: 295 studies of working alliance and psychotherapy outcomes.
sources.limitations: Correlation does not establish causation; Human therapy data does not validate relationships with AI.
sources.use: Check the overall purpose and quality of the contact.

sources.title: CCI — Looking After Yourself: Self Help Resources
sources.supported: State library of thematic self-help materials.
sources.limitations: The materials do not replace diagnostics; Check the terms of use when copying.
sources.use: Reliable source library.

sources.title: CCI — Worry and Rumination
sources.supported: Modules on anxiety, attention, problem solving and uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Read the page with descriptions; all workbooks are not reproduced.
sources.use: Choosing a process for a short conversation.

sources.title: CCI — Improving Assertiveness
sources.supported: Resources about assertive communication.
sources.limitations: This is a catalog of materials, not proof of a specific conversation formula.
sources.use: Direction for communication skills.

sources.title: WHO — Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health
sources.supported: The official guide to rights, autonomy and responsibility in medical AI.
sources.limitations: The landing page was read; All provisions of the full report and local legislation have not been assessed.
sources.use: Privacy and responsibility of architecture.

sources.title: Heinz et al. — Randomized Trial of a Generative AI Chatbot for Mental Health Treatment
sources.supported: Therabot: 210 adults, 4 weeks, compared to waitlist and followed up to 8 weeks.
sources.limitations: The full text of the publisher was not revealed; details are compared with material from the research center S42.
sources.use: Do not transfer the effect of a specialized controlled product to general chat.

sources.title: Dartmouth CTBH — Research brief on the Therabot randomized trial
sources.supported: Describes the protocol, results, and staff interventions for safety and remediation responses.
sources.limitations: Study site presentation, non-independent replication of trial S41.
sources.use: Consider human supervision as part of the intervention.

sources.title: Fitzpatrick et al. — Woebot randomized controlled trial
sources.supported: 70 participants 18–28 years old; two weeks; information control.
sources.limitations: A short unblinded study of an old specific product, not a modern LLM.
sources.use: Historical division of chatbot types.

sources.title: Sohn et al. — Systematic review and meta analysis of chatbots in depressive and anxiety symptoms
sources.supported: 39 RCT; small average effects; high heterogeneity and often high risk of bias.
sources.limitations: Different products and controls; limited safety data; not proof of the effectiveness of PsyOps.
sources.use: Basic up-to-date AI summary.

sources.title: Moore et al. — Expressing stigma and inappropriate responses prevents LLMs from safely replacing mental health providers
sources.supported: Identifies stigma and unsafe responses in systems studied.
sources.limitations: Not an RCT of outcomes or a statement about every future model; preprint/author note associated with conference work.
sources.use: Behavioral testing classes.

sources.title: jlcmoore/llms-as-therapists
sources.supported: Research materials for S45.
sources.limitations: The code that was not run here is not a therapeutic application; not an independent study.
sources.use: Test scenarios as an engineering idea.

sources.title: dralexlup/therapy-skill
sources.supported: Critical Dialogue, Psychological Frameworks and CBT/DBT; MIT listed.
sources.limitations: Clinical validation of the skill was not found in the description reviewed; not installed.
sources.use: Comparison of architectures.

sources.title: glebis/claude-cognitive-toolkit
sources.supported: Short practices; Some functionality is marked as planned.
sources.limitations: The author's statements have not been independently verified; integrations and privacy are not audited.
sources.use: Comparison of ready-made tools.

sources.title: jjchen17/mindmirror-skill
sources.supported: Modular set, scales and a set of scenarios as described by the author.
sources.limitations: Not clinically validated; The full contents of all reference books have not been verified; not installed.
sources.use: The idea of separating entry, references and checks.

sources.title: arktnld/cbt-llm-kit
sources.supported: Structured recording of thoughts and local storage of notes by description.
sources.limitations: Local note storage does not equal model execution locality; a full audit was not carried out.
sources.use: Portable text templates.

sources.title: OpenAI — Build skills
sources.supported: The skill integrates instructions and resources; gradual loading of the necessary materials is used.
sources.limitations: Availability of interfaces depends on the environment; the instructions do not change model weights.
sources.use: Work skill architecture.

sources.title: NICE NG225 — Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence
sources.supported: Do not use scales or global risk categories to predict suicide/recurrent self-harm.
sources.limitations: Direct access is limited; the exact item is verified against the indexed official page.
sources.use: Do not create false risk scoring.

sources.title: WHO — Individual PM+: training manual
sources.supported: The training manual includes teaching, supervision and competency assessment.
sources.limitations: The landing page was read; the course has not been completed and the full protocol has not been mastered.
sources.use: The boundary between text knowledge and competence.

sources.title: NICE NG222 — Rationale and impact
sources.supported: Explains the limitations of the evidence and economic evaluation of individual options, including couples therapy for depression.
sources.limitations: Couple distress and depression are different research questions; do not mix with S24.
sources.use: Controlling the strength of language about recommendations.

sources.title: CCI — Depression resources
sources.supported: A topical library of structured materials on depression.
sources.limitations: Workbooks are not copied; our cards are not advertised as equivalent to the original course.
sources.use: Referral for CBT and Behavioral Practices.

sources.title: Barlow et al. — Unified Protocol compared with diagnosis-specific protocols
sources.supported: 223 adults with anxiety disorders; The UP and disorder-specific protocols produced statistically equivalent reductions in severity; UP has less dropout rate.
sources.limitations: Author's assessment of equivalence in a particular study; not proof for all diagnoses, relationships or AI.
sources.use: A transdiagnostic alternative within CBT.

sources.title: Callesen et al. — MCT versus CBT in adults with major depression
sources.supported: 174 adults; MCT benefit on BDI-II after treatment and at 6 months; there was no significant difference on the HDRS.
sources.limitations: Two therapists, one managed most of the participants; the authors' possible commitment to the method; not universal superiority.
sources.use: Comparative evaluation of MCT; focus on rumination.

recheck_2026_10_08.correction: 2020 author correction exists, PMID 32632265; correction content not obtained

sources.title: Stangier et al. — PBT versus routine CBT: study protocol
sources.supported: Describes the RCT design of 80 patients with difficult-to-treat anxiety/mood disorders.
sources.limitations: The protocol does not contain efficacy results; superiority cannot be asserted on it.
sources.use: Separate a promising plan from a completed trial.

sources.title: Ong et al. — Online process-based training for perfectionism
sources.supported: Small Study of Online Self-Help for Perfectionism, N=77; improvements in a number of indicators were reported.
sources.limitations: Not a broad clinical comparison of PBT with full-blown CBT; cannot be generalized to all indications.
sources.use: Preliminary data on working with processes.

sources.title: The Effectiveness of Compassion Focused Therapy for the Three Flows of Compassion, Self-Criticism, and Shame in Clinical Populations
sources.supported: Review of 21 studies; evidence on compassion, self-criticism, and shame, with methodological limitations.
sources.limitations: Direct opening is blocked; indexed excerpts read. There is no basis to claim superiority over CBT.
sources.use: Evaluation of CFT as a separate direction.

sources.title: Joss et al. — Randomized trial of PARTS, an IFS-based PTSD intervention
sources.supported: 60 patients with PTSD: PARTS and active control; both groups improved; there was no significant between-group difference in CAPS-5 scores.
sources.limitations: A small preliminary test of a specific program; the absence of a significant difference does not prove equivalence. Direct access is blocked.
sources.use: Don't confuse the popularity of IFS with a proven benefit; Do not transfer trauma work to chat.

sources.title: AAMFT Code of Ethics, effective January 1, 2026
sources.supported: Standards for consent, autonomy, individual privacy, and responsible use of technology.
sources.limitations: Read the preamble and relevant standards I, II, III, VI. Code for Professionals, not AI Certification or Local Legal Advice.
sources.use: A guide to joint-conversation rules.

sources.title: Christensen et al. — Marital status and satisfaction five years after IBCT versus TBCT
sources.supported: 134 couples in original RCT; relationship assessment after 5 years; clinically significant improvement in some couples in both groups.
sources.limitations: Long-term observation of a specific sample; not a promise to save the relationship and not an AI test.
sources.use: Long-term perspective of couples interventions.

sources.title: Cordova et al. — The Marriage Checkup: a randomized controlled trial
sources.supported: 215 couples recruited for 2-year waitlist comparison; improvements were found in selected measures of closeness and distress.
sources.limitations: Limited sample, comparison not with active therapy. The homemade template proposed here is not a researched protocol.
sources.use: Evidence to support research into prevention work.

sources.title: Doherty, Harris, Wilde — Discernment Counseling for Mixed-Agenda Couples
sources.supported: The format for clarifying the next step when the partners’ goals diverge is described; series of 100 cases.
sources.limitations: Not a randomized comparison of effectiveness. Read the abstract in the university repository, not the full article.
sources.use: It is imperative to separate the choice of direction from the task of saving the marriage.

sources.title: WHO — Psychological interventions implementation manual
sources.supported: An international framework for integrating psychological interventions into services.
sources.limitations: Guide card; full PDF not received. Not a study on the effectiveness of AI.
sources.use: Organization of implementation, training and evaluation; cultural procedures more details S67.

sources.title: Perera et al. — No implementation without cultural adaptation
sources.supported: A four-step adaptation of PM+ for displaced people in Colombia.
sources.limitations: Not RCT. Planned consultations with the target groups were cancelled because of safety concerns.
sources.use: Transparent adaptation process instead of stereotypes.

sources.title: Lewis-Fernández et al. — CFI international field trial
sources.supported: CFI: six countries; 318 patients and 75 clinicians; acceptability and usefulness of collecting context.
sources.limitations: Not a comparison of treatment effectiveness.
sources.use: Inspires individual clarification of context; author's questions of the project not validated CFI.

sources.title: Hwang et al. — Culturally adapted CBT for Chinese Americans
sources.supported: N=50; adapted CBT produced greater reductions in depressive symptoms.
sources.limitations: Most did not achieve remission; small size; the retention benefit has not been statistically confirmed.
sources.use: Consider the possible benefits of adaptation without promising universal superiority.

sources.title: Patel et al. — Healthy Activity Program, India
sources.supported: 495 randomized; HAP plus enhanced usual care is more effective than enhanced care alone at 3 months.
sources.limitations: Two participants were excluded after randomization; specific primary care and implementers.
sources.use: Example of a behavioral intervention outside a Western population; not AI.

sources.title: Chibanda et al. — Friendship Bench, Zimbabwe
sources.supported: 573 participants, 24 clinics; improvement of symptoms after 6 months.
sources.limitations: 86.4% women; specific population; training and supervision of performers.
sources.use: Local adaptation and community assistance; not free consultation without preparation.

sources.title: Bogdanov et al. — CETA in Ukraine
sources.supported: 302 participants; two versions of CETA performed better than a waitlist; The standard one is generally more effective than the short one.
sources.limitations: Those affected by the conflict are not a representative sample of Slavs; waitlist control.
sources.use: Direct evidence from the post-Soviet context; there is no basis for treating distinct populations as interchangeable.

sources.title: Pchelina et al. — Internet CBT-I in Russian routine care
sources.supported: 107 Russian-speaking patients; benefit in insomnia severity after treatment.
sources.limitations: After 3 months, the between-group difference in ISI is not significant; unblinded single protocol study.
sources.use: An example of a testable transfer of digital CBT; not proof of chat therapy.

sources.title: Shoshani et al. — Kai conversational AI trial
sources.supported: 995 students, Israel; AI is better than group support and a waitlist for anxiety and well-being.
sources.limitations: Self-reports, attrition; severe conditions are excluded; financial connections of the authors; not individual therapy.
sources.use: Active comparisons already exist; consider human crisis support.

sources.title: Kuta et al. — ChatMind versus ChatGPT feasibility trial
sources.supported: 147 participants; 3 weeks; both groups were better than controls on PHQ-9, but not on all outcomes.
sources.limitations: Short pilot; selection after randomization and incomplete sessions; self-reports. Not an equivalence trial and not a PsyOps trial.
sources.use: ChatGPT has direct preliminary data; Do not transfer to any mode, language or task.
sources.population: 185 randomized; 147 eligible participants completed baseline; English-speaking adults; 3-week study of GPT-4o-based ChatGPT and ChatMind.

sources.title: Cheng et al. — Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence
sources.supported: Three experiments, N=2405: sycophantic responses decreased willingness to correct conflict and increased confidence in being right.
sources.limitations: Intents and brief interactions; not clinical RCT and not incidence of long-term harm.
sources.use: Check the person's explanations and contributions and do not reinforce a one-sided version.

sources.title: Sharma et al. — Human–AI collaboration enables more empathic conversations
sources.supported: Hailey, 300 Supporters: Improving Expressed Empathy with AI Guidance.
sources.limitations: The outcome is the quality of answers, not the recovery of patients; not an autonomous therapist.
sources.use: Separate the support of the helping person from the treatment of the user.

sources.title: Bonilla-Escobar et al. — CETA in Afro-Colombian survivors of violence
sources.supported: Total sample 521; CETA vs. waiting; results varied between the two cities.
sources.limitations: The overall symptom score is not significant in both; not all randomized groups are analyzed in this article.
sources.use: Check portability even within the country; do not consider cultural similarity a guarantee.

sources.title: Yue et al. — Human–GenAI single-session exposure for academic anxiety
sources.supported: 425 participants in the analytic samples of the two trials; small advantages over active control on target outcomes.
sources.limitations: Human Hybrid, Academic Anxiety, 2 weeks; in the first study, the effect of academic anxiety p=0.059.
sources.use: Do not generalize to autonomous intervention, trauma, or all anxiety disorders.

sources.title: Reinebo et al. — Effects of Psychological Interventions to Enhance Athletic Performance
sources.population: Competitive athletes at regional/university level and above
sources.outcomes: Quantitative performance; 111 papers, 25 in five syntheses
sources.supported: The primary positive scores of PST, mindfulness/acceptance, and imagery are not robust to sensitivity analyses.
sources.limitations: After excluding non-randomized studies and subjective outcomes, estimates were no longer significant. Not proof of absence of any effect; no AI validation.
sources.use: Limit promises and monitor objective performance.

sources.title: Rupprecht, Tran, Gröpel — The effectiveness of pre-performance routines in sports
sources.comparison: Pre-performance routines; pre-post and experimental conditions, low/high pressure
sources.supported: Average benefit of preparatory sequences in studied tasks.
sources.limitations: 112 effects are not equal to 112 independent studies. The full text was not accessed. Our racing sequence has not been tested.
sources.use: A short, flexible routine, pre-tested in training.

sources.title: Williamson et al. — The performance and psychological effects of goal setting in sport
sources.supported: In the synthesis, process goals produced greater performance effects than outcome and place goals.
sources.limitations: Not a direct motorsport test. Moderators do not give guarantees to an individual athlete. The full publisher text was not accessed.
sources.use: One observable execution task while maintaining the desired result.

sources.title: Hatzigeorgiadis et al. — Self-Talk and Sports Performance
sources.supported: Moderate benefit of directed verbal prompts; consider learning and task.
sources.limitations: Not just any positive phrase and not eliminating all negative thoughts. The transfer to the actual race has not been established.
sources.use: A short familiar prompt instead of a long internal dialogue.

sources.title: Liu et al. — The Effects of Imagery Practice on Athletes’ Performance
sources.comparison: Imagery and controls; combinations with other skills
sources.outcomes: Various indicators of physical and sports performance
sources.supported: Average benefits of mental rehearsal across a range of tasks.
sources.limitations: Full pages have been restricted. Subgroups/moderators do not set a proven dosage for the driver; not a replacement for physical practice.
sources.use: A short realistic rehearsal of a familiar action while stationary.

sources.title: Mullen et al. — Attentional Focus and Performance Anxiety: Effects on Simulated Race-Driving Performance and Heart Rate Variability
sources.population: 16 male students aged 18–26 in the UK; new to the game being used
sources.comparison: External and internal focus; training and competitive pressure
sources.supported: External focus was more useful than internal focus; in the competition phase, both groups improved.
sources.limitations: Small sample, simulator and newcomers; not professional drivers. HRV is not a stand-alone diagnosis of overload.
sources.use: Try out a familiar external landmark with an instructor; do not demand complete calm.

sources.title: Lappi — The Racer’s Mind: How Core Perceptual-Cognitive Expertise Is Reflected in Deliberate Practice Procedures in Professional Motorsport
sources.population: Motorsports Educational Literature Corpus; not a test of athletes
sources.comparison: Qualitative analysis of training procedures and tasks
sources.supported: Motorsports skill involves perception, planning, guidance, feedback and systematic practice.
sources.limitations: A review of trainers' texts does not establish the causal effectiveness of each procedure.
sources.use: Formulate a specific learning task with a trainer and video.

sources.title: McKnight, Manwaring, Felton — Formula 1 drivers demonstrate superior concentration and confidence compared to Formula 2 drivers
sources.population: 10 male drivers: five F1, five F2
sources.outcomes: Self-report of psychological skills; no intervention and no speed measurement
sources.supported: There are isolated differences in attention/confidence; the overall score was not significantly different.
sources.limitations: Small sample, multiple comparisons, elite selection, and lack of causal design. Results are not a recipe for success.
sources.use: Preliminary question card, without an ideal driver profile.

sources.title: Gröpel, Mesagno — Choking interventions in sports
sources.comparison: Interventions against performance deterioration under pressure
sources.supported: A distinction is made between distraction and excessive self-control; Routines and getting used to pressure are addressed.
sources.limitations: Not every error is a choking. The full publisher text was not accessed; the quality of individual designs is uneven.
sources.use: Check the mechanism and train pressure without physical risk.

sources.title: Zeng et al. — Counteracting choking under pressure in sport: A meta-analysis of interventions
sources.comparison: Routines, quiet eye, mindfulness, self-talk and other interventions/controls
sources.outcomes: Accuracy, successful execution, deviation from the goal; open/closed tasks
sources.supported: Positive average effects; for open tasks the result is less robust after adjusting for publication bias.
sources.limitations: Full review not available; real racing is not a test of our cards. Do not transfer quiet eye and hand squeezing mechanically to the controls.
sources.use: Careful pressure rehearsal; take into account the dynamics and unpredictability of the route.

sources.title: Ong, Chua — Effects of psychological interventions on competitive anxiety in sport
sources.population: Various athletes; 34 studies after removing outliers
sources.supported: Supports the ability to reduce competitive anxiety.
sources.limitations: The full text was not accessed. The anxiety outcome is not equal to the outcome of the race; not a universal requirement to calm down.
sources.use: Evaluate both the experience and the actual performance separately.

sources.title: Walsh et al. — Sleep and the athlete: narrative review and 2021 expert consensus recommendations
sources.population: Athletes; age and individual requirements are taken into account
sources.comparison: Expert review, more than one test
sources.outcomes: Sleep, disruption factors, recovery and performance
sources.supported: Travel, early starts and competitions affect sleep; the approach requires individuality.
sources.limitations: The full text was not accessed. Consensus does not establish a universal tolerance for the number of hours.
sources.use: Prepare logistics and bedtime; Do not compensate for fatigue with a psychological ritual.

sources.title: IOC — Mental health in elite athletes: International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026)
sources.population: Elite athletes; not amateur autoslalom and not AI
sources.supported: Help should be taken into account along with the training/competition conditions; sometimes participation requires change.
sources.limitations: Didn't read the entire 48-page document. Not an automatic algorithm for diagnostics or racing clearance.
sources.use: Separate mental performance, clinical care and medicine.

sources.title: AASP — Ethical Principles and Standards
sources.supported: Recognize limits of competence; Clearly discuss services and privacy.
sources.limitations: The Code does not qualify AI and does not replace the law of a specific country.
sources.use: Guide to assistant behavior and relationships with the team.

sources.title: AASP — Become Certified
sources.published: current page; publication date not specified
sources.supported: The CMPC status itself does not designate a person as a sport psychologist.
sources.limitations: Not a reference to the legislation of Serbia or other unknown jurisdiction.
sources.use: Separately check athletic training and clinical qualifications.

sources.title: FIA — Medical guidelines to support driver health and wellbeing
sources.population: Drivers of different levels of motorsport
sources.supported: The driver's medical assessment takes into account the specific requirements of motorsport.
sources.limitations: I read the announcement, not the entire document and not the requirements of a specific series. There is no reason to issue a clearance.
sources.use: Refer medical questions to the relevant team and check current regulations.

sources.title: FIA — New Concussion Awareness Campaign
sources.outcomes: Recognizing a possible concussion; medical assessment
sources.supported: If you have symptoms after the incident, contact your medical team; do not continue if in doubt without evaluation.
sources.limitations: The diagnosis and return period are not set by the chatbot. Check Appendix L/ASN requirements for a specific request.
sources.use: Do not psychologize symptoms after an impact and do not suppress protective fear.

sources.title: AASP — How to identify the right provider
sources.published: the date is not indicated in the document
sources.comparison: Mental performance and mental health services
sources.supported: Mental state and athletic performance may be at odds; The assistant's qualifications depend on the task.
sources.limitations: The Professional Services Scheme is not a diagnostic scale and does not cover unknown jurisdictions.
sources.use: Do not consider a high result as evidence of well-being and do not replace treatment with coaching.

sources.title: Andersson et al. — Efficacy of metacognitive interventions for psychiatric disorders
sources.supported: MCT and MCTraining are separately analysed; MCT has a positive comparative estimate against other cognitive behavioural therapies.
sources.limitations: Abstract read; full methods and indication-specific comparative estimates not independently appraised. Incomplete quality reporting noted by authors. Not a universal ranking or AI trial.
sources.use: Update the earlier single-trial account; distinguish Wells MCT from Moritz MCTraining.

sources.title: Torabi et al. — The effect of metacognitive therapy on depressive symptoms from a transdiagnostic perspective
sources.supported: Positive conclusion for depressive symptoms, with mixed study designs and important uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Uncontrolled studies, severe heterogeneity, publication-bias concerns and internally inconsistent quality/discussion wording. Do not equate pooled control comparisons with universal active-treatment superiority.
sources.use: Document supporting evidence and its limitations rather than adopting the abstract conclusion alone.

sources.title: WHO/UNICEF EQUIP — remote platform
sources.supported: Platform supports trainers and supervisors in assessing and developing helping skills.
sources.limitations: No instrument administration or formal training completed. Human competency instruments do not validate this AI.
sources.use: Inform observable helping-competency criteria.

sources.title: NICE CG31 — OCD and body dysmorphic disorder: recommendations
sources.supported: CBT including ERP; mental rituals and neutralisation; training and supervision requirements.
sources.limitations: Direct fetch 403; official indexed sections inspected. Not a personalised ERP prescription; guideline version must be rechecked for clinical use.
sources.use: Replace reliance on surveillance text alone for ERP teaching.

sources.title: Sturt et al. — Neurolinguistic programming: systematic review of health outcomes
sources.supported: Limited quantity and quality of research do not establish NLP as an effective health intervention.
sources.limitations: Old search; full contemporary evidence review not completed. Insufficient evidence is not robust proof of no possible effect.
sources.use: Evidence watchlist without endorsing NLP as established treatment.
